title: The two read operations, their resource and element names and their error status set are stated by no source, because the legacy read was an in-process Java interface with no path, no query parameter and no status code
source: Legacy RWB-E2-008 section 12 'Published interfaces called' (List<PaymentView> RecoveryDataApi.paymentsLoaded(LocalDate businessDate), LocalDate RecoveryDataApi.nextInstallmentDate(String accountKey), BatchStatus BatchStatusQuery.forSource(String sourceSystem, LocalDate businessDate)) and section 4 steps 2 and 3; legacy section 14 MSG-P1-001; RWB-P1-E1015-APP (MSG-P1-001 and MSG-P2-007 as published by the freshness story); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 15 and 41 (the P1 API surface); TSD P1 T-A.1 and T6.2; _work/msr/wp/B-P1-08.md contract list of RWB-P1-E2008-APP (RWB-P8-E2008-CON only); Template and Rules v1 §R5.5 DP-11 and DP-13 and §R9
section: 1 Story; 3 Preconditions; 4 Flow steps 3, 6 and 8; 5 Exception paths X1, X2, X5, X6 and X7; 7 Acceptance criteria AC1, AC2 and AC5; 12.1; 13 Configuration and reference data; 14 Validation and messages
description: The legacy read carried a business date in Java and answered a list of PaymentView, a LocalDate and a BatchStatus, so nothing in the sources fixes a REST shape for the split. Four things are open and the last one reaches the run. (1) The resource names and paths of the two reads, which no source document carries. (2) The query parameter `businessDate`, the account key as a path segment and the element names of the two answers (PaymentsAnswer, PaymentFact, BatchStatusStamp, ProductStamp, InstallmentFacts), which this service has to publish and RWB-P8-E2008-CON has to consume. (3) The status set and the problem body (400, 401, 403, 404, 409, 503), where the legacy interface threw exceptions and no status code existed. (4) The held answer itself, 409 with MSG-P1-001 and MSG-P2-007, which no source names, while MSG-P2-007 is a case-creation text in FSD P1 and this story renders it for a payment-matching run with its waiting count. The story cannot settle the last two alone, because the run's contract declares the shapes it consumes and its error handling depends on them.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-008 section 12 code block 'List<PaymentView> RecoveryDataApi.paymentsLoaded(LocalDate businessDate);' and 'LocalDate RecoveryDataApi.nextInstallmentDate(String accountKey);'; legacy section 4 step 2 'reads the payments posted for business date D from v_ace_payment through the P1 interface'; legacy section 14 MSG-P1-001 '{product} is from {date}. Today's load has not arrived.'; RWB-P1-E2008-APP section 12.1 'The resource names, the two query parameters and the element names of the two answers: the legacy read was an in-process Java interface with a business date argument and no path, and no source document carries a payments or installment-facts path'; RWB-P1-E2008-APP section 14 'the rendering of MSG-P2-007 for a payment-matching run rather than a case-creation run is not stated by any source'
owner_role: Solution architect with the P8 contract owner
proposed: Publish the two operations on /api/recovery/source-data/v1 with the resource names, the `businessDate` query parameter, the element names and the status set of section 12.1 in the OpenAPI fragment of the service baseline; take the consumed rows of RWB-P8-E2008-CON from that fragment at the wave 2 contract freeze and record the same shapes in the next version of the API Specification; confirm with the P1 message owner that MSG-P2-007 renders the payment-matching run and its waiting count.

title: FSD P1 A2.2 stamps a payment read on DP01 Account and arrears while the Work Package slice note names DP05, and no source states whether the read or the rwb-payment run answers a held business date
source: FSD P1 A2.2 (DP01 Account and arrears accounts for `v_ace_payment`); TSD P1 T3.4 and T3.7 (DP01 is fed by ALS); the story line and slice note of RWB-P1-E2008-APP in _work/msr/wp/B-P1-08.md (DP05 named beside a read that carries no payment); RWB-P1-E1015-APP (`data_product_load`, the LOADED and STALE states, MSG-P1-001 and MSG-P2-007); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 43 row 26 and slide 44 row JOB-07 (the run starts on `AceDataReady`); legacy RWB-E2-008 section 3 ('P1 has stamped DP01 for the business date and published AceDataReady (EV-26)'), section 5 X3 and section 7 AC5; Template and Rules v1 §R5.5 DP-05, DP-09 and DP-10 and §R9
section: 1 Story; 3 Preconditions; 4 Flow steps 2 and 8; 5 Exception paths X1 and X2; 7 Acceptance criteria AC1, AC2 and AC5 and the Target reading; 8 Business rules BR3; 9 State transitions; 12.1; 12.8; 13 Configuration and reference data
description: Two questions meet on the same read and neither is answered by a source. (1) Which stamp gates the payments: FSD P1 A2.2 gives `v_ace_payment` to DP01 Account and arrears and TSD P1 T3.7 feeds DP01 from ALS, while the Work Package slice note names DP05 beside the same read and DP05 carries no payment row; the story holds the gate on DP01 and carries the ALS batch row in the answer, which is its own choice and not a sourced value. (2) Who refuses a held business date: the legacy row X3 stopped JOB-07 before it ran, and after the split the read's gate and the run's start condition watch the same batch and the same stamp, so one condition can be refused twice, once as a 409 from this read and once as the run's own stop, and no source says which is the refusal of record or what the read answers to a caller that should never have been started. Nothing states either how far the DP01 stamp and the ALS batch row of one business date may disagree before the read refuses, which decides whether an empty day can be answered for a date whose batch is complete but whose product is stale.
evidence: RWB-P1-E2008-APP section 7 Target reading 'AC1 also names the product the rows were read under: DP01 accounts for `v_ace_payment` in FSD P1 A2.2 and is fed by ALS in TSD P1 T3.7, and the slice note names DP05, which reads no payment, so the gate is held on DP01 and the answer carries the ALS batch row beside it'; RWB-P1-E2008-APP section 7 Target reading 'Who answers that hold — this read or the run that is started by `AceDataReady` after the same condition — is not settled by any source'; legacy RWB-E2-008 section 5 X3 'The ACE batch for ALS is not COMPLETE for the business date | JOB-07 does not run; no missed payment is raised from stale data'; legacy RWB-E2-008 section 7 AC5 'Then JOB-07 does not run for business date 2026-12-15'
owner_role: Solution architect with the P1 data product owner
proposed: Hold both gates on DP01 Account and arrears and answer 409 with MSG-P1-001 for the product and the date of the load in use and MSG-P2-007 for the held run, with no row of any kind; record DP05 as not the stamp of a payment read and correct the slice note in the Work Package and the data product map in the next version of FSD P1 A2.2; state in RWB-P8-E2008-CON that the run's own refusal for the business date is its own and that the read's 409 is the answer to a call made anyway.

title: The order of the payment answer, the fold of a repeated payment_code, the row cap of one call and the number of ALS payments per business date are stated by no source
source: Legacy RWB-E2-008 section 8 BR6 ('One proceeds row per payment_code'), section 13 ('add unique index ux_proceeds_payment_code on (payment_code)'), section 7 AC6 and section 4 steps 2 and 9; TSD P1 T3.4 (the `v_ace_payment` columns and their types); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 11 (one hop) and slide 15; _work/msr/wp/B-P1-08.md story line of RWB-P1-E2008-APP; Template and Rules v1 §R5.5 DP-11 and §R9
section: 3 Preconditions; 4 Flow steps 4 and 10; 5 Exception paths X3, X4 and X5; 7 Acceptance criteria AC1, AC3 and AC6 and the Target reading; 8 Business rules BR1 and BR8; 12.1; 12.8; 13 Configuration and reference data
description: The legacy job read a list and wrote rows, so no source fixes the order of an answer, the grain of a read or how many rows one call may carry. (1) The order: `paymentCode` ascending is the story's choice, and no source states an order for the legacy `paymentsLoaded` list, so a caller that compares two answers of one business date depends on a rule only this contract carries. (2) The fold: the monolith's unique index made one proceeds row per `payment_code`, which says nothing about two `v_ace_payment` rows that share a code and differ in amount or `data_as_of`, and no source says which row the read answers or whether the duplicate is a data-quality break instead. (3) The cap: no source states the volume of ALS payments for one business date, so the story answers one business date or one account per call, unpaged, with the cap as configuration, and leaves unanswered what the read does when a date would exceed it, since a truncated page, a 413 and a 409 are all undefined. The reconciliation count of REC-04 is the only volume fact in the sources and it is a daily control, not a read limit.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-008 section 13 'add unique index ux_proceeds_payment_code on (payment_code) where payment_code is not null'; legacy section 8 BR6 'One proceeds row per payment_code; one PaymentMissed per plan and due date'; legacy section 7 AC6 'the proceeds table still has 2 rows for business date 2026-12-14'; RWB-P1-E2008-APP section 12.1 '(3) The row cap of one call: both reads answer one business date or one account in one call and are unpaged, with the cap as configuration, because no source states the volume of payments per business date'; RWB-P1-E2008-APP section 5 X4 'The same `payment_code` appears twice in a read | One row is answered and the second is folded into it'
owner_role: Tech lead with the P8 contract owner
proposed: Publish one row per `payment_code` ordered by `paymentCode` ascending, both reads unpaged with the cap as configuration, and name the fold rule in the OpenAPI fragment and in RWB-P8-E2008-CON; record in the next version of the API Specification what a call answers when the cap would be exceeded, and route the duplicate `payment_code` to the REC-05 break list of RWB-P1-E1011-APP rather than to this read if the data-quality owner confirms it is a break.

title: Architecture v5 slide 15 names a GET /accounts/{id} of rwb-source-data that TSD P1 T-A.1 does not carry and no Work Package owns, while this story answers nextInstallmentDate
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 15 and slide 41 (the P1 API surface); TSD P1 T-A.1 (the operation list) and T3.4 (DF-ACE-028 `v_ace_account.next_installment_date`); legacy RWB-E2-008 section 3 ('The next due date of each plan account is read from v_ace_account.next_installment_date at the same business date') and section 12 (`LocalDate RecoveryDataApi.nextInstallmentDate(String accountKey)`); _work/msr/wp/B-P1-08.md (no story of the Work Package owns an accounts read); Template and Rules v1 §R5.5 DP-13 and §R9
section: 1 Story; 3 Preconditions; 4 Flow step 6; 5 Exception paths X5; 7 Acceptance criteria AC2; 12.1; 12.8; 13; 19 Out of scope
description: `nextInstallmentDate` has two possible homes and neither is settled. Architecture v5 slide 15 names an account resource of this service whose `GET /accounts/{id}` would answer the account, while TSD P1 T-A.1 carries no such operation and no Work Package story owns one; the legacy interface answered the date as a bare `LocalDate` from `v_ace_account`, which is the shape this story keeps on its installment-facts read. Three things are therefore open: whether the account resource is published in wave 2 at all, whether the installment facts are a sub-resource of the account or an operation of their own as published here, and who owns the account read if it is published, since a fourth P1 story would have to be created or the operation attached to an existing one. If the account read is published later and answers the date, the field moves, the run acquires a second call for one business date and its 2 s budget covers two hops instead of one.
evidence: RWB-P1-E2008-APP section 7 Target reading 'AC2 answers `nextInstallmentDate` here although Architecture v5 slide 15 also names a `GET /accounts/{id}` of this service that TSD P1 T-A.1 does not carry and no Work Package gives an owner, so the field may move to that operation when it is published'; RWB-P1-E2008-APP section 19 'The `GET /accounts/{id}` operation that Architecture v5 slide 15 names: if it is published, `nextInstallmentDate` may move to it from this story\'s installment read'; legacy RWB-E2-008 section 12 'LocalDate RecoveryDataApi.nextInstallmentDate(String accountKey); // P1, over v_ace_account'
owner_role: Solution architect with the P1 tech lead
proposed: Keep `nextInstallmentDate` on the installment-facts read of this story and record the account resource of Architecture v5 slide 15 as unowned and unpublished in the API Specification; if the account read is commissioned, give it an owner in the P1 service epic and move the field in one contract change, with the field of this operation deprecated in the same change and RWB-P8-E2008-CON aligned to it.

title: The caller of both reads has no actor of record after the data-load actor was retired, and the architecture names the P8 to P1 call as a Temporal activity while the Work Package fixes one REST hop
source: TSD P1 T6.2 (roles and rights held as data in rwb-access and reached through its authorise contract; the SY-DATALOAD data-load actor is retired); legacy RWB-E2-008 section 10 ('The recovery service identity, JOB-07 | Runs JOB-07, calls the rule evaluator and reads the ACE views (Write-off and posting U)') and section 4 step 1; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 15, 17, 41 and slide 44 row JOB-07; _work/msr/wp/B-P1-08.md story line of RWB-P1-E2008-APP (the call is REST); Template and Rules v1 §R5.5 DP-10 and DP-11 and §R5.4 class C and §R9
section: 3 Preconditions; 4 Flow steps 1 and 3; 5 Exception paths X8; 7 Acceptance criteria AC5; 10 Authority; 12.1; 12.5; 12.9; 13 One sentence per pattern; 17 Guardrails
description: Two unstated things meet on the same call. (1) Who calls: the legacy run acted as 'the recovery service identity, JOB-07' with Write-off and posting U, rights are now held as data in rwb-access and reached through its authorise contract, and the SY-DATALOAD actor that loaded the data is retired with no source naming its replacement for a run that now lives in rwb-payment; so whether the workload identity of the run holds Platform administration R on a refusal, whether the run receives a 403 or a 409, and whether a refused read is visible on the run's own monitor at all are not stated. (2) How it travels: the architecture describes the P8 to P1 step as a Temporal activity of the run's workflow, while the Work Package and DP-11 fix one REST hop with a 2 s budget, and the two readings differ in who owns the retry, the timeout and the idempotency: if the activity wraps the REST call, retries belong to the run and a retry is harmless because both reads are idempotent; if P1 were to implement the activity, P1 would take a Temporal dependency none of its patterns carries. The story builds the REST reading and records the other as open.
evidence: RWB-P1-E2008-APP section 3 'the SY-DATALOAD actor is retired and no source names its replacement for the run of JOB-07'; RWB-P1-E2008-APP section 13 'the architecture also names the P8 to P1 call as a Temporal activity, which is recorded as open because the Work Package fixes REST'; RWB-P1-E2008-APP section 12.5 'Both reads are synchronous REST steps that answer in one call with a 2 s budget, and this story starts no workflow and no activity'; legacy RWB-E2-008 section 10 'The recovery service identity, JOB-07 | Runs JOB-07, calls the rule evaluator and reads the ACE views (Write-off and posting U)'
owner_role: Solution architect with the P8 tech lead and the P4 owner
proposed: Take the caller as the payment-matching run of rwb-payment holding a workload identity token, with a refusal readable by the data steward and the platform administrator under Platform administration R, and record the run's own operator in the authority table of RWB-P8-E2008-APP; settle the P8 to P1 step as one REST hop wrapped by the run's Temporal activity, correct the activity description in the next version of the Temporal Workflow and Activity Catalog, and keep this service free of a Temporal dependency for the two reads.

title: The data product code and the source system label an answer names are reference data, and the reference-data contract is not in this Work Package's contract list
source: Template and Rules v1 §R5.5 DP-07 (reference-data contract of rwb-case, H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON and C RWB-P3-E1043-CON), §R3 default ruling on reference data and §R9; TSD P1 T3.4 and T3.7 (DP01 is fed by ALS); RWB-P1-E1001-APP and RWB-P1-E1015-APP (`data_product` and `data_product_load`, the DP01 row and its name); legacy RWB-E2-008 section 3 ('P1 has stamped DP01 for the business date') and section 12 (`BatchStatus BatchStatusQuery.forSource(String sourceSystem, LocalDate businessDate)`); _work/msr/wp/B-P1-08.md contract list of RWB-P1-E2008-APP (RWB-P8-E2008-CON only)
section: 1 Story; 3 Preconditions; 12.1; 12.2; 12.8; 13 Configuration and reference data; 17 Guardrails
description: Both answers name two reference values, the data product code DP01 with its name 'DP01 Account and arrears' and the source system ALS, and DP-07 gives reference data to the contract of rwb-case through the client library. This Work Package lists only RWB-P8-E2008-CON for the story, so neither the platform contract nor the P3 contract is on it and the story builds against the client library and a fixture. Three things are open: whether the data product list and the source-system list are served by the reference data of rwb-case at all, since the data products are rows of this service's own `data_product` table written by RWB-P1-E1001-APP and stamped by RWB-P1-E1015-APP, which would make P1 the owner of its own list rather than a consumer of P3's; whether the name of a product is a column of that list or is composed from the code; and what an answer does when a code has no list row, which the fixture of section 12.8 carries while no criterion and no exception path fixes its answer.
evidence: RWB-P1-E2008-APP section 3 'the Work Package lists no reference-data contract for this story, so they are a library read with a fixture until that contract is published'; RWB-P1-E2008-APP section 12.8 'Product code fixture | The reference-data client library | DP01 and DP13 with their names for the fixture, the source system ALS, and one code with no list row'; Template and Rules v1 §R5.5 DP-07 'Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON'; _work/msr/wp/B-P1-08.md story line of RWB-P1-E2008-APP 'C: ["RWB-P8-E2008-CON"]'
owner_role: Business analyst, P1 with the P3 reference-data owner
proposed: Add RWB-P3-E1043-CON to the contract dependencies of this story at the wave 2 contract freeze and serve the data product list and the source-system list from the reference data of rwb-case; until it is published, build against the client library and the fixture of section 12.8 and keep the gap open against the story. If the data product list is confirmed as this service's own `data_product` rows, record that ruling in the Ownership Map and in the FSD P1 data product section instead and drop the dependency.
